text:
Maria.AE: Heads up 1 BlueHarbor POC (internal name: coralfall). They want to run coraline-30b inside their datacenter with KV prefix caching and customer HSM. Asking for compat checklist, rough lead time, and a 10 qps cost ballpark. Any red flags?

Tony.SE: First pass: can coraline-30b be served with q8_0 path? I recall coraline has RMSNorm + grouped_gemm kernels. @Olivia.ML any conversion notes?

Olivia.ML: Quick note: original coraline-30b uses grouped_gemm + RMSNorm and a custom rotary setup. We can quantize to q8_0 but current runtime release lacks the optimized grouped_gemm kernel so perf will be worse until we recompile with the kernel patch. Conversion + compile + basic perf test = ~3 business days. KV prefix caching works for prefixes up to ~2048 tokens without change; beyond that we should discuss kv-sharding.

Kyle.Infra: Requirements for on-prem: NVIDIA driver >=525, CUDA >=12.1, and PKCS#11 userland libraries if they plan to attach HSM. If they supply A100S vs H100 makes a big perf and memory diff. Also need container runtime >= 1.6 for our shim. I'll open an infra validation ticket.

Maria.AE: They said they can provision either 2x A100S or 4x H100s. They want enterprise SLA + 24/7 support. Are we comfortable offering that for Private?

Tony.SE: Dedicated SLA is standard at 99.95%. Private SLA/supported uptime is negotiated; we usually do platform fee + managed support for higher SLAs. Cost estimate: hosted 4x H100 equivalent ~ $420-480/hr platform (rough); Private will add license/platform + ops. I'll run the 10 qps estimate and SOW stub.

Ollie.Security: We support customer HSM via PKCS#11 in Private using our KMS adapter. Deliverables we provide: SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summary, network/dataflow diagram, and DPA. If they require model residency with zero egress, we'll need to validate storage encryption at rest and keywrap behaviour. Please have them fill the security questionnaire.

infra-bot: INF ticket created: INF-8472. Steps to validate on customer host:
```
./check_cuda.sh --min-version=12.1
ldconfig -p | grep libpkcs11
kubectl apply -f redwood-driver-check.yaml
```

Tony.SE: On the model side, if timeline is tight we can propose coraline-lite (~13B distilled) which is far cheaper and runs on 2x A100s easily. Quality tradeoff is modest for many QA/use cases.

Olivia.ML: Onboarding timeline (internal estimate): conversion + quantize + compile + initial bake = 3 days. KV stress and perf tuning = 1 day. Integration checks + docs = 1 day. Canary rollout adds another 1-2 days. Total ~5-6 business days from greenlight, assuming infra checks pass.

Maria.AE: Action items: I'll request driver/CUDA output, PKCS#11 presence, and completed security RFI. Tony please prepare the 10 qps cost calc and SOW draft. Olivia tentatively reserve 2 days for conversion after greenlight. Ollie I'll DM RFI once they send. Thanks :thumbsup:

Tony.SE: Will prepare numbers. If they choose Dedicated vs Private the delta could be large; will include both scenarios.

Olivia.ML: FYI if they need absolute lowest latency we should prod on H100s and ensure kernel patch applied. Without it latency may spike.

Maria.AE: Great, I'll report back when I have their env dump and RFI.
